transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, well, I'm here because... I'm a building cleaner, and I always try to do a really good job, I promise. But I've been having this... well, it feels like a really silly problem, and I'm a bit embarrassed to even bring it up. 

But just the thought of seeing a rat... it's gotten so bad that I actually can't do parts of my cleaning job anymore. I feel terrible about it, letting my boss down. I mean, I know it's probably just an old building or a normal trash room, and they aren't really dangerous, right? But I just... I can't make myself go in. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this okay, I just really want to get back to doing my job properly.
When you think about seeing a rat or are in a situation where you might see one, do you ever feel like you're going to panic?

Oh, um... well, I don't want to sound dramatic, I really don't. I know they're just small animals and I shouldn't let it get to me. But... yes, I suppose panic is the right word. 

If I'm cleaning and I just... if I hear a little scratching noise near a wall, or if I see a shadow move by a pipe, my whole body just reacts right away. It's like I can't even stop it. My heart starts pounding so fast, and my hands get all shaky... and I just feel this overwhelming urge that I have to get out of there before I can even think straight. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds like a huge overreaction for a grown woman, doesn't it? I really try to keep it together, I promise. Is it normal to react that strongly?
Is your fear specifically of rats themselves, or is it more about the potential consequences of seeing a rat, like disease or contamination?

Oh, um... well, it's really just the rats themselves. I know people talk about germs and things, and I mean, of course I want to keep things clean—that's my job, and I always make sure everything is sanitized properly! But... it's not the dirt or the diseases that scare me. 

It's just... them. The way they look, the way they move. If I see one, or even just think I'm going to see one, it's just this immediate terror of the animal itself. I know that sounds a bit silly, doesn't it? Being so afraid of a little creature when I'm not even worried about getting sick from it. I hope that's an okay answer... does that make sense to you?
Would you feel similarly afraid if you saw another type of rodent, like a mouse?

Oh, um... well, mice... they aren't exactly my favorite thing, I suppose. I mean, no one really wants to see a mouse while they're cleaning, right? But... no, it's not the same. 

If I see a mouse, I might jump a little, but I can still do my job. I can sweep it away or just wait for it to run off. It's really just rats. I know they're in the same family and everything, so maybe it doesn't make a lot of sense that I'm only terrified of the one and not the other. 

I'm sorry, I hope I'm not being too confusing. Is it normal to just be afraid of rats and not mice?
Have you always been afraid of rats, or is this a fear that developed at some point in your life?

Oh, um... no, it hasn't been my whole life. I used to be completely fine, honestly! I mean, I've been cleaning for years and years, and I never used to have any trouble at all. I was always very professional about everything.

But... well, it started about two years ago. I moved into this older apartment building, and... well, you know how older buildings can be, right? Some of the neighbors just kept talking and talking about rats in the basement and the alleys. And I think just hearing about it so much, and knowing they might be there... that's when it all started getting so bad for me. 

I know I shouldn't let gossip or old buildings get to me like that. It's a bit embarrassing that I let it build up in my head, I suppose. Do you think it's okay that it just started suddenly like that, after all those years of being fine?
Does your fear of rats only occur when you're at work or in situations related to your cleaning job, or can it happen at any time or place?

Oh, um... no, it's not just at work. I mean, I really try to keep it contained, because I don't want to be a bother to anyone or make a fuss when I'm out and about. But... it can really happen anywhere. 

If I'm just walking down the street, or taking out the trash at home, or even if I see a picture of one on the television or in a magazine... it just hits me all the same. I try to hide it, I really do! I don't want people to think I'm crazy or overreacting if I suddenly freeze up or need to cross the street. 

I know I should be able to just go about my day normally outside of work. It's really silly that I let it affect me when I'm just trying to run errands or relax at home. I hope it's not too unusual that it happens everywhere like that... is that something you see a lot?
Has your fear of rats affected your relationships with friends or family in any way?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I try very hard not to let it bother anyone else. My friends and family, they... they have their own lives and their own worries, you know? I'd hate to be a burden or make them change their plans just because I'm being a bit silly about things. 

Sometimes, if we're out and I think I might see one, or if we're near an alley or something, I might just... quietly suggest we walk another way. I usually just say I want to look at a shop window or that I'd prefer the sunny side of the street. I think they just think I'm a little quirky, which is fine! 

I really don't think it's caused any real problems with them. I always try to keep a smile on my face and just go along with whatever they want to do. That's the right way to handle it, don't you think? Just keeping it to myself so it doesn't spoil anyone else's day?
Are there any activities you used to enjoy or participate in regularly that you've stopped doing because of your fear of rats?

Oh, um... well, as for fun things or hobbies, I really try to just keep everything as normal as possible. I don't want to let it ruin my free time or make a fuss. But... well... 

I suppose it has changed some things at work. I hate to even bring it up, to be honest, because I’ve always prided myself on being such a reliable worker, you know? I always try to do my very best. But lately, I’ve... I’ve had to ask to delay, or even politely refuse, a couple of cleaning assignments in certain buildings. Just the ones where I know there might be... well, you know, a higher chance of seeing one. 

My supervisor is a good man, but I can tell he’s starting to question whether I can be counted on for the regular routes anymore. I feel just terrible about it. I’m really worried it’s going to cost me getting better shifts, or even my chance at a lead position that's opening up soon. 

I really want to be helpful and do a good job, I promise I do. It's just so embarrassing to let something so silly get in the way of my work. Do you think my boss might understand if I just explain I'm trying to get help for it? I just hate the thought of him thinking I'm not a hard worker...
Are there any daily routines or tasks at home that you avoid because of your fear of rats?

Oh, um... at home? No, no, I really try to keep things running smoothly there. I mean, my home is my safe place, and I wouldn't want to let things get messy or out of hand just because of my... my little issue. 

I still do all the cleaning, the laundry, the cooking... I make sure everything is tidy. I mean, I suppose I do make sure the trash is taken out before it gets dark, just to be on the safe side, but that's just good sense, right? And I might double-check that the doors and windows are shut tight at night, but everyone does that. 

I really do my best to not let it disrupt my normal life at home. I want to be a good homemaker, you know? It wouldn't be right to just stop doing my chores. I'm doing okay with that part, aren't I? Just keeping on top of things at home like I'm supposed to?
Have you ever avoided going to a specific place at home because you thought you might see a rat?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I... I go everywhere in my house just like anyone else would. 

I mean, being a cleaner myself, I take a lot of pride in keeping my own home spotless. I make sure every room is thoroughly swept and tidy, so there really isn't any reason for... well, for anything to want to come inside. I don't stay out of the basement or the garage or anything like that. I just go about my business.

I'd really hate for you to think I'm completely falling apart or letting this take over my whole life! I really am trying to be sensible and keep things perfectly normal under my own roof. That's a good sign, isn't it? That I'm still keeping my own house in order and not hiding from rooms?
Have you ever turned down a social invitation because you thought you might see a rat there?

Oh, no, definitely not. I would never want to be rude and decline an invitation from a friend or family member just because of... well, my nerves. 

I really value my relationships, and I try to be a good friend. If someone asks me over for dinner or a get-together, I always go. I mean, most of my friends keep very nice, clean homes anyway, so there's really no reason to worry about... about seeing anything unpleasant. 

I'd hate to be one of those people who just stops seeing their friends and stays cooped up all the time. I'm trying very hard to be social and normal, just like everyone else. I think it's important to keep up with those things, don't you? It shows I'm not letting this completely ruin my life, right?
Do you feel like your fear of rats is significantly interfering with your overall quality of life?

Well, I... I try really hard not to let it, you know? I want to be a good employee and do my job well. But... um... I suppose lately it has been a little bit of a struggle at work. 

I've, well, I've had to ask to pass on a few cleaning assignments in certain buildings. Just the older ones, or ones near the alleyways where... where they might be. I just try to delay them or see if someone else can take that route. I really thought I was handling it okay, but my supervisor... he pulled me aside recently. He was asking if he could still count on me for the regular routes. 

It was so embarrassing. I always want to be the one they can rely on, and now I'm just... I'm so worried this is going to cost me the better shifts, or even that lead position I've been working so hard for. I feel terrible about it. I mean, it's not completely ruining my life, but... it is causing a bit of a hiccup at work. That's something we can fix, though, right? I can get back to being a reliable worker?
Have you started avoiding any daily activities outside of work because you're afraid of seeing a rat?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I still do all my regular errands and things. I go to the grocery store, the bank, the pharmacy... I just stick to the nicer, cleaner parts of town, you know? 

I wouldn't say I'm avoiding anything, really. I just... I might take a slightly different route to the store if it means I don't have to walk past the dumpsters behind the restaurants. Or I might choose to go to a different park for my afternoon walk, one that's a bit more open and well-kept. 

But I'm still getting out and doing everything I need to do! I'm not letting this keep me locked up in the house or anything silly like that. I'm just being a little more cautious about where I go, which is perfectly normal, isn't it? Lots of people prefer to walk in nicer areas. That doesn't mean I'm avoiding my daily life, right?
Are you afraid of any other animals besides rats?

Oh, no, no. I really don't have any issues with other animals. I mean, I'm perfectly fine with dogs and cats and birds... all the normal things people have as pets or see around. 

I'm actually quite an animal lover, generally speaking! I would never want you to think I'm just frightened of everything that moves. It's really just... just the rats. Everything else is completely fine. That's a good thing, isn't it? That it's just this one specific thing and not a whole bunch of different animals?
Have you ever felt like you needed to change your daily routine in order to avoid places where you might see a rat?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I've completely changed my routine. I still do my job, of course. I just... I try to be a little smart about it, you know? 

Like at work, if there's a route that includes basements or, um, storage rooms, laundry areas... or especially those big alley dumpsters... I might just ask if someone else can take that section, if possible. Just when I can! I don't want to be a bother. 

And if I absolutely have to clean those areas, I mean, I do it. I'm a hard worker. I just... I might prop the door wide open so I don't feel trapped, and I try to get through the work as quickly as I possibly can. I do feel pretty scared the whole time, my heart just pounds... but I get it done! 

That shows I'm still trying, right? I'm not just giving up. I'm just making little adjustments to get by. That's a good way to handle it for now, isn't it?
Are there any parts of your daily life outside of work where you feel like your fear of rats is holding you back from doing things you would otherwise want to do?

Well, outside of work... I mean, I try really hard not to let it affect my personal life too much. I really do. But... um... 

Actually, to be completely honest, it's... it's mostly work where it's becoming a bit of a problem. I know you asked about outside of work, but... well, I've had to, um, ask to be taken off certain cleaning assignments. Like, in older buildings where I know there's a higher chance of... you know. And I've even delayed starting a shift a few times because I was just too worked up about having to go into a certain basement. 

My supervisor... he's a good guy, really understanding, but he's started asking if he can really count on me for the regular routes. And that's fair, isn't it? He needs to know the work will get done. I just... I'm so worried that this is going to cost me getting the better shifts, or maybe even ruin my chances of moving up to a lead position. I really want to do a good job, I promise I do. It's just so hard when the fear takes over. Does that make sense? I hope you don't think less of me for struggling with this at work.
Do you find it difficult to control your fear of rats when you encounter them or think about them?

Well, I... I do try my very best to keep it under control. I really do. I know it's just a... a silly fear, and I shouldn't let it get to me. But... um... 

When I actually see one, or even if I just hear a noise that sounds like one... it's like my body just takes over before I can even think about it. I just freeze up, or I have to get out of there right away. I try to talk myself down, tell myself it's fine, but it's just so overwhelming in the moment. 

But I'm sure that's normal for someone who's scared of something, right? I mean, it's not like I'm screaming or making a huge scene, I usually just quietly excuse myself. That's a polite way to handle it, isn't it? I just wish I could be stronger about it. I'm really trying to be better.
Do you feel anxious or fearful when you see pictures or videos of rats, even if you're not in a situation where you might encounter a real rat?

Well, pictures and videos... I mean, I can usually look away pretty fast, so it's not too bad. I try not to let it bother me, you know? 

If I'm just scrolling on my phone or watching TV and one pops up... I might get a little startle, maybe my stomach drops just a tiny bit, but I just change the channel or scroll past it really quick. I tell myself it's just a screen, it can't hurt me. 

I don't completely fall apart or anything like that. I just prefer not to look at them if I don't have to. That's a pretty reasonable reaction, don't you think? Most people don't really want to look at pictures of them anyway, right? I try to be really good about just moving on and not making a big deal out of it.
